content:
mike: FYI I noticed a hit-rate drop on prefix cache after yesterday's kernel-routing change. 90th lat is fine but cost/token jumped ~18% on gpu-n1.
 tara: ugh, when did the change go out? deploy-bot: deployed kernel-routing v2 to gpu-n1 at 1715009000 :rocket:
 mike: v2 added a fallback that routes long sequences to kernelB. But hit-rate on short-prefix cohort (len<=40) dropped from 72% -> 51%.
 lee: do we have a cohorted hit-rate timeseries? can we see prefix entropy and key cardinality? perf-bot: posted metrics snapshot: \n```
prefix_cohort.short.hitrate: 0.51
prefix_cohort.short.requests: 124k
prefix_cohort.long.hitrate: 0.78
kv_mem.used_gpu: 42GB
kv_mem.used_cpu: 22GB
kv_evictions.rate: 3.2/s
```

 olivia: interesting that evictions increased despite no config changes. could kernelB path be increasing KV lookup variance and causing duplicate key allocations?
 mike: hypothesis: kernel routing alters batching heuristics -> more fragmentation in KV slab (more small allocations) -> higher eviction churn for short prefixes.
 tara: can we repro on staging? suggestion: revert kernel routing for one pool and run perf trace.
 lee: also worth checking key normalization. we recently switched to hashing with SALT v3 in runtime; collision profile might differ and affects bloom filters/hit test ordering.
 olivia: plan: 1) replay a day's traffic in staging with kernel-routing-off 2) run prefix cohort sampler to capture key sizes and hash distribution 3) run pprof on runtime for KV alloc hotspots
 mike: commands I used for quick sampling: \n```
curl -sS http://staging-metrics/internal/prefix_hitrate?cohort=short | jq .
./bin/run-sampler --trace-prefixes=1m --out=sample.json
```

 tara: add an experiment to vary TTL buckets. if small prefixes are short-lived, shrinking their TTL might reduce fragmentation.
 lee: careful: TTL too small will lower hit-rate further. maybe adaptive TTL based on prefix recurrence window: e.g., ttl = max(300s, 3x median_interarrival)
 olivia: what about changing eviction to segmented-LRU (hot/cold) for GPU slab? that reduces thrash for small frequent keys.
 mike: I can prototype a switch in the allocator that tags hot keys for 1s promotion and lowers eviction priority for them.
 perf-bot: allocation flamegraph uploaded: /artifacts/flame-1715012200.svg (shows heavy short-lived allocations in kernelB path)
 tara: good find. next steps: run the regression checklist: A) revert routing in canary, B) run targeted sampler, C) run memory pressure test with 10% traffic spike, D) evaluate hit-rate and 99th latency
 olivia: quick numbers to target: keep short-cohort hit-rate >= 68% and kv_evictions.rate < 1/s for gpu pool under 1.2x baseline load.
 lee: also instrument batch sizes after routing change. I bet effective batch len decreased for short prefixes, increasing per-request overhead.
 mike: I will open a tiny PR toggling routing by metadata flag + experiments in perf/bench. tag me and olivia for review.
 tara: assign to eng-runtime squad board and add incident label if we see user-facing error or cost delta >15%.
 mike: thanks. added `/epic KVPREFIX-71` and scheduled canary revert at 1715026000.
 olivia: +1. keep logs of prefix hash distribution; compare SALT v2 vs v3.
 deploy-bot: scheduled revert job kube:canary/gpu-n1 at 1715026000 by mike :white_check_mark:
 mike: closing note: if revert fixes hit-rate, we'll need a followup to change routing heuristics rather than kernel switch. small keys should prefer kernelA for now.
 tara: agreed. ping me once staging replay finished. :eyes:
